title: Gfpt1/HBP suppression induces a selective ER and integrated-stress program with recurrent Ogt repression
exact_observed_result: Gfpt1 perturbation induced ER and integrated-stress transcripts in selected classes while repeatedly repressing Ogt. The largest response was in 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c cells, with 311 FDR<0.05 rows including Ogt down and Herpud1, Asns, Cyb5r1, Ddit3, Hspa5, Chac1, and Oga responses.
biological_interpretation: GFPT1/HBP suppression is read out as a selective neuronal ER/ISR liability that couples UDP-GlcNAc stress to compensatory ER folding and O-GlcNAc pathway genes, rather than as a uniform brain-wide response.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

support.description: A strong 151 TH response and smaller hypothalamic, midbrain, and cortical responses share stress induction with Ogt repression; several planned cortical and hippocampal classes are buffered.

caveats: The packet title lists cortical classes that are weak compared with the dominant 151 TH and caudal/subcortical responders.
Pvalb, CA3/CA2/DG, and NP/CT/L6b/OB examples had zero FDR<0.05 rows and are best treated as buffered or unengaged.

prior_expectation.summary: GFPT1 is rate-limiting in the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway producing UDP-GlcNAc for N-glycosylation and O-GlcNAcylation; HBP deficiency has been linked to ER stress.
